ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of Korea, Articles 18, 28, 255 and 635 (Yuhan Hoesa registration and name clearance); Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Articles 4 through 6 and 14 (customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, suspicious transaction reporting); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Act on Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information; Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) examination and reporting standards; Supreme Court Commercial Registration Matters Processing Rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (equivalent of Certificate of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office under the Supreme Court of Korea, in the court district where the Yuhan Hoesa's principal office is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary -> Apostille certificate issued by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Hague Apostille member states; parallel track for non-member states: notarization -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (official certified copy of the Korean commercial register showing active status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office under the Korean Supreme Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notary certification of the certified copy -> Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states: Korean notary certification -> MOFA authentication -> destination-embassy consular legalization only. Use only one path depending exclusively on the destination state's Hague membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the local representative and counsel to execute incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA and the appointed Korean representative, with Korean notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signatures and board minutes by a Korean notary -> Apostille by MOFA if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille state; otherwise -> notarization -> MOFA certificate -> consular legalization by the receiving state's consular officer in Korea. No both-path sequencing is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation) including the Korean entity name, registered office, purpose and share structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and shareholders of the Yuhan Hoesa, filed and registered at the Korean Commercial Registry and notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean notarization of the articles -> Apostille by MOFA for Hague states; for non-Hague states, Korean notarization -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization at the destination state's consulate; the consular path must not be added after an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the future corporate bank account of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing Korean commercial bank, signed by a branch manager and compliance officer with bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean bank signature and seal notarized by a Korean notary -> Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention jurisdictions; for non-member jurisdictions, notarized bank signature -> MOFA authentication -> consular legalization by the destination country's embassy or consulate in Korea. The two authentication methods are parallel alternatives, never a chain.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding and ongoing CDD must screen all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, authorized signatories and commercial counterparties against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) regulations, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs counter-terrorism and anti-proliferation designations, U.S. OFAC SDN and 50% affiliate rules, EU targeted financial sanctions, UK OFSI, and other applicable local lists. PEP screening covers foreign and domestic heads of state, senior executive, judicial and military officials, domestic and international organization leaders, state-owned enterprise executives, and their family members and close associates. The semiconductor wholesale transaction profile, including cross-border high-value SSD and CPU shipments, Swift TT and escrow inspection wires, source of funds, invoice authenticity, logistics documents, third-party payments and shell-company patterns, must trigger enhanced due diligence. Refresh screening every 90 days, upon material changes, and before every new jurisdiction or counterparty; retain all evidence at least five years after relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iROS) at iros.go.kr and the Korean Commercial Registration Name Search and Registration portal of the local District Court Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean law requires the legal name of a Yuhan Hoesa to be expressed in Korean Hangul and to end with the statutory legal-form designator 'Yuhan Hoesa'. An English auxiliary trade name may be used commercially, but every tax invoice, bank mandate, customs filing and commercial contract must quote the exact registered Korean name. Romanized or Chinese-character side names must be consistent with the Korean registration and may not replace Hangul. The four-tier naming hierarchy is: (1) a distinctive personal or trade element; (2) a business-purpose descriptor for wholesale electronic components and semiconductor devices; (3) the legal-form suffix identifying limited liability; and (4) a unique disambiguating marker when the first three tiers collide with an existing registered name. The registry will reject identical, deceptively similar or confusingly similar existing names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, counsel must obtain the written statement of refusal from the Commercial Registry, isolate the prohibited or conflicting token, prepare an amended distinctive element and promptly refile a new name-clearance application; there is no automatic extension and, if the 30-day reservation window lapses, the company reverts to an unprotected name. If the applicant disputes the registrar's legal conclusion, local counsel shall file a written objection with the Registry Office within 14 days under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching evidence of prior trademark rights, coexistence consent or statutory non-confusion. A further appeal lies to the competent District Court and, ultimately, administrative litigation before the Administrative Court within 90 days of final refusal; the same procedure remains available to oppose a later-conflicting registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a wholesale SSD and CPU trading company, the National Tax Service and Korean commercial banks generally reject a bare virtual mailbox or mail-forwarding address. A serviced office may be accepted only if there is a physically identifiable suite, lease agreement in the exact Korean registered name of KR_YUHANGHOESA, signage, dedicated telephone line, local staff presence and accessible transaction records. Even if the registry tolerates a virtual office, banks may decline or restrict the current account, tax authorities may deny the issuance of electronic tax invoices, and the entity will be flagged as lacking commercial substance in the electronic-components industry. A shared desk without exclusive possession and a named lease is not bankable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is moderate, approximately 35%, within the first year for a dedicated wholesale office; it rises to about 70% for a virtual-only address and falls below 10% when the company maintains a real office with local personnel and physical records. The NTS and municipal authorities may inspect for: Korean-language name-plate matching the registration, actual employees, VAT and electronic tax invoice system access, lease and utility contracts, server and communications equipment, commercial correspondence, third-party logistics records, inventory or supply contracts for SSD and CPU products, and evidence of management decision-making. All registered-office records must be available at the registered address during business hours.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 601 et seq. governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) formation, registered office, capital contribution, corporate officers, and commercial registration; supplemented by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act where foreign shareholders remit subscription funds.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, with electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) at i.roj.kr; in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (notarized) and the corporate incorporation registration application submitted to the court registration office, together with the capital payment certificate and officer acceptance certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. Nevertheless, the entire subscribed contribution stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be paid in full into a blocked capital escrow account at an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank before the incorporation registration filing. The escrowed funds cannot be withdrawn or used until the company obtains its certificate of incorporation registration. If a foreign investor remits funds from abroad, a foreign exchange declaration is required; if the investment is reportable under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, foreign investment notification must be filed through KOTRA Invest Korea or an authorized foreign exchange bank before the deposit. The official state filing fee field is reported as zero only because the fee is variable by capital; actual registration tax of 0.4% of paid-in capital, local education tax of 20% of registration tax, and court fees are payable at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA. WHEREAS, the incorporator and all subscribing members of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, have proposed to establish the Company for the lawful business of open-market brokerage, wholesale and distribution of solid state drives and server processors under ISIC 4651; WHEREAS, the initial contribution capital has been subscribed in full in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and must be paid into a dedicated capital escrow account maintained at an authorized foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea before the incorporation registration is filed; WHEREAS, the Company will maintain its registered office in the Republic of Korea and will accept legal service of process and official correspondence at such registered office; WHEREAS, the Company intends to conduct cross-border wholesale payments through Swift TT and Escrow Inspection Wire rails, requiring corporate bank account authorization and anti-money laundering controls; WHEREAS, the Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act require the appointment of statutory officers and the adoption of governance documents; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Payment. The subscription of the initial contribution capital is hereby ratified and confirmed. Management is directed to deposit all subscribed funds, in full, into the capital escrow account at an authorized foreign exchange bank and to deliver the bank payment certificate to the registration authority together with the incorporation filing. 2. Registered Office. The registered office shall be adopted as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, namely the address identified in the registered office proof, and the directors are authorized to execute lease consents and file all address notices required by the court registration office. 3. Banking and Payment Authorization. The chief executive officer and the finance director, acting jointly, are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute Swift TT and Escrow Inspection Wire payment instructions, sign online banking agreements, verify beneficiary details, and maintain all AML and KYC records required for the Company's medium-risk semiconductor trading profile. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the Company: the chief executive officer, the finance director, and the compliance and AML responsible officer. Each officer shall sign a written acceptance, provide identity documents for registration, and cooperate in the corporate seal registration procedure. 5. Foreign Investment Reporting. Counsel is directed to file any required foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and to complete all foreign exchange declarations with the authorized bank. 6. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in force until amended by a subsequent board resolution. All requisite signatures and corporate seals have been affixed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Execution of Notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) at i.roj.kr and a licensed notary public in the district of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before formation, conduct a legal-name search in the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office to ensure that the proposed name Yuhan Hoesa and its authorized English display name do not collide with an existing Korean legal entity. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act, stating the exact corporate name, the business purpose of open-market brokerage of solid state drives and server processors, the registered office address, the aggregate contribution capital, the number of statutory officers, and the term of existence. The incorporators and all subscribers must execute the Articles in person or by duly notarized power of attorney. A licensed notary public must notarize the Articles, and the notary's acknowledgment certificate must be appended before the court filing. The notarized Articles become the controlling constitution document and may not be amended before incorporation except by a separate notarial deed. Submit the notarized instrument to the IRO for provisional name verification or, where the registry requires, submit the paper court filing.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate name search request in the IRO
Passport or national identity document of each incorporator and subscriber
Alien registration certificate or Korean visa for foreign resident subscribers
Notarized power of attorney if a professional agent acts
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean, fully executed
Notarial certificate of the Articles of Incorporation
Proof of proposed registered office address, such as lease consent or ownership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the proposed name as identical or confusingly similar, select a secondary name and file a fresh name clearance. If the notary refuses acknowledgment due to incomplete identity proof, cure the issue by producing authenticated passports and revised signatures. If an administrative query is raised, respond in writing within seven days; if the application is suspended, resubmit the corrected notarized instrument with the applicable re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Blocked Escrow Account Creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea, such as KEB Hana Bank, Shinhan Bank, Kookmin Bank, or Woori Bank, with corporate and foreign-exchange dealing capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital escrow account in the future corporate name, designated as Yuhan Hoesa in incorporation. The authorized representative must present the notarized Articles, complete the bank's corporate account application, and deposit the full subscribed contribution capital in cash before the incorporation registration filing. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, verify beneficial owners, classify the AML risk profile, and request source-of-funds documentation. If funds are remitted from abroad, the remitter must file a foreign exchange declaration and, where applicable, a foreign investment notification under FIPA. The bank must issue a capital payment certificate or deposit balance certificate stating the exact amount held. The account is blocked and no withdrawal is permitted until the company is duly incorporated and a new corporate operating account is opened. Any discrepancy between the deposited amount and the capital stated in the Articles will cause rejection at the court registration office.
required_dossiers: Application form for the provisional capital payment account
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or identity document of the authorized representative
Pre-registration corporate seal or company seal declaration
Foreign exchange declaration and FIPA notification number for overseas remittances
Source-of-funds evidence, including three months of bank statements or tax records
Beneficial ownership declaration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide certified source-of-funds statements and a signed AML undertaking. If the deposit is below the subscribed capital, top up the account before registration. If the bank quarantines an overseas remittance, provide the SWIFT confirmation and notarized ownership documents; if unresolved, select another authorized foreign exchange bank and rerun the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office for the registered office district, or the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) for electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate incorporation registration application together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate issued by the escrow bank, the statutory officers' acceptance certificates, identity evidence, registered office address proof, and payment of registration tax and local education tax. The court will examine whether the corporate purpose is lawful, whether the Articles are validly notarized, and whether the paid-in capital has been properly evidenced. Upon acceptance, the court registers Yuhan Hoesa in the commercial register, issues the incorporation registration certificate and corporate seal certificate, and the company acquires juridical personality. The filing must be made in the court district where the registered office is located, and the application forms must be completed in Korean. Electronic filing through the IRO is permitted and provides a case number for tracking.
required_dossiers: Corporate incorporation registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate from the authorized bank
Statutory officer acceptance certificates and identity copies
Corporate seal registration application
Proof of registered office, such as lease agreement or ownership deed
Registration tax and local education tax payment receipts
Power of attorney if filed by legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, cure the stated omissions, such as seal inconsistency or missing landlord consent, within the court's statutory deadline. If the application is dismissed, prepare a fresh application and pay the new filing fee. If the refusal is based on unlawful business purpose, amend the business description by notarial deed and refile with additional legal justification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), accessible through the Home Tax Service online portal at www.hometax.go.kr, or the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation is completed, file an application for business registration for corporate income tax and value-added tax. The applicant must present the incorporation registration certificate, the original corporate seal, the CEO's identity document, and evidence of the registered office lease. The NTS will verify the business classification as wholesale of computers and peripheral equipment under ISIC 4651, issue the business registration certificate, and assign the corporate registration number, which also serves as the VAT tax invoice number. The company must register its electronic tax invoice issuance system and obtain a certified tax invoice seal. For open-market wholesale brokerage of solid state drives and server processors, no separate manufacturing or industrial operating license is required at this stage. If later importing or exporting physical semiconductor goods, additional customs registration under the Customs Act will be required, but the present trading scope remains subject only to ordinary tax registration.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Incorporation registration certificate
Corporate seal and corporate seal certificate
Passport or identity document of the CEO or statutory representative
Registered office lease agreement or ownership deed
Articles of Incorporation
Bank account confirmation or future operating account details
Electronic tax invoice issuance service application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the business classification or requests an address inspection, submit a supplemental lease certificate and floor plan. If rejection results from a mismatch between the Articles and the requested tax business type, file a correction application with the NTS. If the business registration certificate is delayed beyond the SLA, escalate through the Home Tax Service civil petition channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation, AML/KYC Completion, and Payment Rail Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate banking center of the selected authorized bank, together with the bank's Anti-Money Laundering compliance team under the supervision of the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration certificate, business registration certificate, Articles, the First Board Resolution approving bank signatures, and the corporate seal certificate to the bank. Complete the beneficial ownership register, KYC questionnaire, and AML risk classification appropriate for a medium-risk semiconductor wholesale trading profile. The bank will set the dual-authorization matrix for Swift TT and Escrow Inspection Wire payments, issue corporate electronic banking tokens, and establish transaction thresholds for high-value SSD and CPU settlements. The compliance officer must retain all client due diligence files, screen counterparties against sanctions lists, and maintain transaction records for the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. After activation, the company may execute escrow inspection wires only when the underlying trade contract, inspection certificate, and payment instructions are attached and signed by the two authorized officers.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration certificate
Business registration certificate
First Board Resolution approving bank signatures and payment matrix
Signature specimen and corporate seal certificate
Beneficial owner identification and source-of-funds documentation
AML questionnaire and risk classification form
Board resolution for Swift TT and Escrow Wire authorization
Passports and alien registration cards of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's AML/KYC unit rejects the application due to insufficient source-of-funds information, provide an independent legal opinion, audited financial statement, or negative news clearance. If a payment is quarantined after activation, submit the supporting trade contract, packing list, insurance certificate, and inspection report. If the bank continues to decline the transaction, open an account at a second authorized foreign exchange bank and repeat the KYC procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. For the current ISIC 4651 wholesale-brokerage scope, no industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing license is required. If the company later operates physical warehousing, the competent authority will be the local Metropolitan City or Do office responsible for warehouse business registration under the Warehouse Industry Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. ISIC 4651 wholesale of computers, computer peripheral equipment, and software is not a licensed manufacturing or chemical activity under the Korean Industrial Development Act or Occupational Safety and Health Act. The ordinary business registration certificate issued by the National Tax Service is sufficient for the described open-market brokerage of solid state drives and server processors.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division; Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. No Full Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration is required because the current activity is limited to wholesale brokerage without a physical project site, factory, assembly line, chemical process, or industrial installation. If the company later constructs or operates a logistics warehouse above statutory thresholds, a small-scale environmental review under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act may become mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The wholesale brokerage activity produces no wastewater discharge, VOC emission, air pollutant release, or hazardous waste generation. If damaged SSD or processor inventory is later treated as electronic waste, the Wastes Control Act requires storage, transport, and recycling through a licensed waste handler, and untreated discharge to sewerage or uncontrolled landfill is prohibited.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at present. A pure wholesale brokerage office does not require a Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval. If the company later opens a storage room or warehouse, it must obtain fire-fighting system installation approval under the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Management of Fire-Fighting Systems, comply with the mandatory structural load requirements of the Building Act, and satisfy the general duty to provide a safe workplace under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, operated through the Home Tax Service online portal at hometax.go.kr, with customs administration performed by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Yuhan Hoesa in Korea must first complete commercial registration at the District Court having jurisdiction over the domestic registered office and obtain the Certificate of Registered Matters and certificate of corporate seal. Within 20 days from the day following business commencement, the entity must file the Business Registration Application with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The application package must include the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, shareholders registry and board resolution authorizing the Korean foreign-invested company setup, passport and identity documents of the foreign shareholder and the statutory representative, a power of attorney appointing a local tax representative, proof of the domestic office address such as a lease agreement or certificate of building registration, and, where applicable, the foreign investment report certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Upon approval, the District Tax Office issues the Business Registration Certificate containing a single 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified Korean Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT identification number used for corporate income tax, VAT, wage withholding tax, and all national tax compliance. After issuance, the entity must activate an electronic tax invoice profile in the Home Tax Service and register the local tax representative in the system. For a foreign non-resident corporation with no fixed domestic place of business but nevertheless carrying on a Korean VAT-taxable activity, the NTS operates a special simplified VAT registration procedure for foreign business operators, and foreign suppliers of electronic or digital services to Korean consumers may register through the Home Tax Service dedicated non-resident VAT registration channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation under the Commercial Act and is per se classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act, subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment, no beneficial ownership transparency election is available for Korean tax purposes, and profits distributed to shareholders are separately subject to dividend withholding tax. The corporate tax liability is borne by the entity, not by the shareholders, and no territorial elective exemption is permitted for wholesale trading income; treaty relief, if any, applies only through the relevant income tax treaty and mutual agreement procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not maintain a check-the-box or elective entity-classification regime with respect to a domestically incorporated Yuhan Hoesa, and no hybrid mismatch election is available in the domestic statute. Hybrid mismatch consequences are to be addressed through the OECD BEPS inclusive framework and the applicable tax treaty using the competent authority and mutual agreement procedure where such double non-taxation or double deduction would otherwise arise.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary threshold applies to VAT registration in Korea; every business operator that supplies goods or services is required to register with the competent tax office within 20 days from the day following business commencement. The narrow statutory exclusion from registration for an individual small business with no fixed place of business and prior-year gross turnover below KRW 10 million is not available to the Yuhan Hoesa corporate entity or to the ISIC 4651 semiconductor wholesale brokerage activity, and therefore the Korean LLC must obtain a VAT Identification Number as part of its Business Registration Certificate without regard to anticipated turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered business operators engaged in B2B supplies must issue an electronic tax invoice through the NTS Home Tax Service, and the electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the National Tax Service no later than the day following the date of supply. The NTS operates a centralized e-tax-invoice clearing and validation system that verifies the Business Registration Number of both parties, reconciles issued and received invoices, and cross-matches declaration data with customs clearance records from UNI-PASS and foreign exchange receipt data from regulated Korean banks. Korea does not deploy real-time physical fiscal stamping devices, but the Home Tax Service electronic tax invoice system acts as a mandatory anti-fraud clearing mechanism and triggers automated risk scoring for unusual export transactions, zero-rated invoice patterns, and delayed or missing e-tax-invoice transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 20(1) of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods are subject to VAT at the rate of zero percent. For the wholesale export of solid-state drives and server processors, the Korean exporter must establish that the goods physically left Korea pursuant to a customs export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, that title and risk passed to a non-resident purchaser under the commercial contract, and that the consideration was paid in a foreign currency through a Korean foreign exchange bank. Qualifying offshore services, including digital or technology services supplied to a foreign service recipient outside Korea, may also qualify for zero rating where the services are consumed abroad and the consideration is received in foreign exchange, provided the statutory documentation is maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration confirmation or export clearance certificate accepted and recorded through UNI-PASS
Original bill of lading, sea waybill, or air waybill evidencing physical shipment outside Korea
Inward remittance certificate from a Korean foreign exchange bank confirming receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Export sales contract or purchase order setting out the parties, goods, quantity, price, and INCOTERMS
Bank foreign exchange transaction report and, where applicable, foreign exchange purchase certificate showing the disposition or repatriation of proceeds
Supporting correspondence and insurance documents demonstrating a genuine cross-border trade transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service conduct selective and post-clearance audits of zero-rated export transactions by reconciling customs export declarations, electronic tax invoices, bills of lading, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If a zero-rating claim is unsupported or the underlying export is determined to be fictitious, the National Tax Service will reclassify the supply as taxable domestic supply, assess VAT at the standard 10 percent rate on the export price, impose additional tax for late or underpaid VAT and for false or incomplete tax invoices under the Value-Added Tax Act, and add national tax interest and surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes. In cases involving intentionally false tax invoices, fabricated customs declarations, or fraudulent claims for refunds, the matter is referred to criminal enforcement under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the entire VAT refund is clawed back together with interest, penalties, and potential criminal fines and imprisonment for responsible parties. Exporters must therefore retain the statutory documentation bundle for the full tax statute-of-limitations period and ensure that all export proceeds are repatriated to Korea within 180 days from the date of export declaration acceptance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalised current account and capital account regime, but the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes reporting, designation, and approval requirements for certain cross-border flows. The Korean won (KRW) is convertible for trade and non-trade current account items, including international wholesale semiconductor transactions, provided the underlying economic substance is proven through customs declarations, invoices, and contracts. Capital account transactions, such as foreign direct investment, loans, and securities dealings, generally operate under a prior notification or post-reporting framework; however, large-scale fund transfers or changes in beneficial ownership can trigger enhanced review by the Bank of Korea and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEBRIS). Profit repatriation through dividends is permissible once corporate tax is settled and audited financial statements are filed, but banks may request evidence of the original invested capital, tax clearance certificate, and board resolution. Surrender of export proceeds is not mandatory on a fixed percentage basis, but exporters are required to settle eligible current account receipts through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank and report the collection method, amount, and overdue status within 30 days after the collection deadline. For a spot semiconductor wholesale trader, maintaining a robust documentary trail is essential because the BOK can request the underlying transaction documents to confirm the absence of disguised capital flows, third-party settlement without commercial rationale, or trade-based money laundering. The regime is therefore best described as fully convertible for legitimate trade but subject to granular reporting, monitoring, and periodic compliance audits, making adherence to statutory reporting timelines a non-negotiable treasury function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Presidential Decree No. 32770), Korean exporters are not required to surrender export proceeds to the Bank of Korea; they may retain foreign currency in a domestic foreign exchange bank account. However, the exporter must ensure that all export proceeds are collected within a statutory term of 90 days from the loading or export declaration date, extendable up to 180 days with a prior report, and must be received through a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea. The full amount of the export proceeds must be reported via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEBRIS) within 30 days of actual collection. No mandatory conversion of foreign currency into KRW is imposed for export receipts; conversion is at the discretion of the entity. Non-resident-owned Korean entities are subject to the same settlement rules, and any delay beyond the statutory period without a valid delay report may result in penalties of up to 50 million KRW or criminal sanctions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW & USD)
Capital Escrow Account + Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW, USD, EUR)
Capital Escrow Account + Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW & USD)
Capital Escrow Account + Trade Settlement Account for LC and Collection

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI (electronic money institution) cross-border viability is very low for a Korean-resident non-bank entity. Under the Korean Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Specific Financial Transactions Information Act, only licensed financial companies (banks, securities firms, or registered electronic financial business operators) may provide foreign exchange transfer or deposit-like services. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) does not issue standalone EMI licences for non-resident fintech firms; offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut Business cannot service Korean-domiciled business accounts without partnering with a local licensed bank and obtaining a report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Operating an offshore EMI directly as the primary clearing rail would be considered an unlicensed foreign exchange business in Korea, exposing the entity to regulatory sanctions, bank account freezes, and potential criminal liability. A pragmatic arrangement is to use a foreign currency account at a Tier-1 Korean bank for settlement, while using an offshore EMI only for auxiliary low-value disbursements outside Korea, provided payments do not touch the KRW system and all underlying trade documentation is retained for the Korean bank's compliance review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean LLC (Yuhan Hoesa) with non-resident shareholders, physical presence of all statutory directors at the bank branch is generally required for initial account opening unless the bank allows a remote onboarding process through a Korean notary public or a domestic attorney-in-fact under a power of attorney. Most Tier-1 Korean banks (KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori) mandate at least one director or officer with signatory authority to appear in-branch in Korea, while non-resident shareholders may complete remote overseas KYC via a Korean consulate or an apostilled certificate of corporate existence. The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations and Korean anti-money laundering regulations require banks to verify the identity of at least one natural person who controls the legal entity; therefore, a physical presence of the authorised representative is likely. A remote consular proxy opening is possible only if the bank has an approved 'non-face-to-face account opening' procedure, which is rare for corporate accounts with trade-related AML-risk. In practice, we recommend a two-step approach: (1) a power-of-attorney holder physically visits a selected branch for the interview and document certification, and (2) the non-resident beneficial owners provide notarised and apostilled passport copies plus a video call with the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involves non-resident shareholders deemed politically exposed persons (PEPs) from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) a certified extract from the Korean corporate registry (등기사항전부증명서) showing the exact shareholding percentages, (b) for each PEP, a sworn source-of-wealth statement covering severance taxes, dividend receipts, and asset sale proceeds, (c) audited financial statements or bank references from the PEP's current relationship bank for the preceding two fiscal years, (d) a notarised memorandum explaining the commercial role and expected trade volumes of each shareholder, and (e) a professional risk assessment from a Korean AML compliance advisor confirming no unexplained funding sources.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export declaration value mismatches or suspicious invoice pricing for SSD/CPU wholesale trades, indicating potential trade-based value manipulation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare: (a) signed sales contracts and master purchase agreements with third-party price references, (b) OEM/CPU serial number traceability logs and packing lists, (c) originals of the Korea Customs Service export declaration (Export Declaration Details) and the associated customs trade statistics showing the HTS code (8471.70.5050 for SSDs and 8542.31.0000 for processors), (d) two independent market pricing valuations from reputable semiconductor distribution indexes (e.g., DRAMeXchange, TrendForce), and (e) a complete logistics trail including air waybill, Bill of Lading, and terminal receipt confirming the physical movement of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement requests where payment is directed to a non-counterparty entity or through a jurisdiction unrelated to the end-customer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) a group corporate register and shareholding relationship chart explaining the third-party payee role (e.g., parent collection hub or factoring company), (b) a tripartite set-off agreement or inter-company netting agreement with legal opinions from a Korean law firm and the counterparty jurisdiction's counsel, (c) the original export contract containing a clause permitting assignment of receivables, (d) letters from the ultimate buyer confirming consent to the settlement route, and (e) bank statements of the third-party payee for the prior six months if the payee is not a regulated financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent amendments to export inward remittances with repeated 'advance payment' and 'refund' circular flows, creating a typology of disparate volume patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: (a) a treasury policy that documents the purpose of advance payments (e.g., rolling prepayment for urgent spot shipments), (b) a chronological log of MT103 payment messages with SWIFT UETR, corresponding invoice numbers, and delivery milestones, (c) internal email approvals from the compliance officer for each amendment, (d) a reconciliation report signed by the external auditor confirming that all prepayments are fully absorbed within 60 days of shipment, and (e) a commitment letter from the Korean bank's designated relationship manager acknowledging the amendment pattern and the bank's prior due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound investment into KR_YUHANGHOESA, the non-resident shareholder must first file a foreign direct investment report (FDI report) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or a designated Korean bank. The Korean bank will issue a certificate of foreign investment (외국인투자신고확인서) after verification of the share capital, remittance sources, and ultimate beneficial owner. Funds must be remitted through a SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's bank to the entity's capital escrow account held at one of the Tier-1 domestic banks. The remittance purpose code must be 'Foreign Direct Investment' (code 3200) and the narrative should reference the FDI report number. Inward FX transactions exceeding USD 200,000 may be subject to an automatic receipt report to the Bank of Korea via FEBRIS; there is no prior approval requirement for a bona fide FDI. Capital verification (자금관리/자본금 검증) is handled by the bank and the foreign exchange broker, with the bank issuing a Foreign Exchange Demand Confirmation. The Korean entity must deposit the injected capital into a 'tax clearance account' and cannot disburse the funds until the bank's KYC review is fully completed. The entire capital transfer trail must be archived for at least five years, including the F/X contract, bank-certified report, share subscription confirmation, and the approval of the board of directors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade disbursements, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for TT settlements, supported by the Korean 'Trade and Commerce Payment' purpose code (e.g., code 1210 for exports). For large or structured chip wholesale deals, the Korean bank will advise a commercial letter of credit (LC) as the most compliant rail, with the Korean entity as the beneficiary and the foreign buyer's bank issuing an LC. The entity must use the BK (back-to-back) LC or open a seller's guarantee if acting as intermediary. Documentary collections (D/P, D/A) are acceptable, but they carry a higher AML-review burden because the bank must confirm the underlying transportation documents. The treasury must ensure that all outbound wires include the exact trade invoice number and purchase order reference in the beneficiary information; any mismatch can trigger a 5-day compliance hold. For Korean won payments to domestic suppliers, the entity can use the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC)-based payment system or the bank's virtual account; however, this is not cross-border and is outside the FX reporting scope. Cross-border payments must be settled in USD, EUR, or JPY as established in the trade contract; KRW is not an official settlement currency for third-country trades unless explicitly permitted by the bank under a KRW offshore settlement agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts are permissible only if the underlying exposure is evidenced by a real trade forecast or existing receivable/payable up to 12 months. The bank will require the entity to submit a valid tax invoice and a signed export/import contract; speculation is prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for Korean residents on KRW cross-rate because KRW is a deliverable currency; however, if the underlying is USD/CNY or USD/EUR exposure arising from third-country procurement, the bank may allow an outright forward in those currencies only when the contract legs are fully booked with non-KRW settlement.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) are permissible only for medium-to-long-term debt or investment flows, not for short-term wholesale trading. The entity may enter into a rolling FX swap (외국환스왑) for up to 180 days with a Tier-1 bank, but the bank will treat the swap as a loan-equivalent facility and require collateral or a credit limit.

Options are allowed only for hedging committed future FX cash flows; the entity must submit a hedging policy signed by the CEO and an annual utilisation schedule to the bank. The bank will reject any instrument designed to create a synthetic KRW exposure outside the reporting system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Supporting Financial Statements (including local income surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, no later than 31 March of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the determined corporate tax (40% for fraudulent non-filing); ordinary under-reporting is subject to a 10% penalty and fraudulent under-reporting to a 40% penalty; late payment accrues a statutory daily surcharge of approximately 0.022% from the day after the deadline. Persistent non-filing leads to estimated assessment, enforced collection, business registration cancellation, and after extended dormancy a court-ordered deemed dissolution and registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return and Payment for both statutory six-month filing periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January to June): file and pay by 25 July. Second half (July to December): file and pay by 25 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or under-reporting attracts VAT-specific additional taxes of 10% to 40% depending on the nature of the noncompliance, plus daily late-payment surcharges at the statutory rate; repeated delinquency results in NTS enforced collection, seizure of assets, and cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Members' General Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's registered office / Members' Meeting record kept in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the meeting and approval must occur by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, inspect, approve, or preserve the financial statements, audit reports, and minutes is a Commercial Act violation subject to an administrative non-criminal fine of up to KRW 5 million, and it gives the company a defective corporate-governance record that may trigger a qualified or adverse audit opinion and loss of tax reserve benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing with the Financial Supervisory Service (if statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Signed external audit report must be lodged with the FSS within 2 weeks after the members' meeting approval of the audited financial statements, and no later than 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the company fails to appoint an external auditor when required, the Financial Services Commission may designate one at the company's expense; failure to submit the audit report is subject to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Corporations and will render the financial statements unusable for statutory, credit, and regulatory purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Status Report and UBO/Equity Transfer Change Report (if foreign-invested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA and/or the designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual status report by 31 March of the following year for a 31 December fiscal year-end; any transfer of membership interests or change in foreign investor/beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual status report or 30-day change report may result in administrative fines, loss of foreign-investor tax exemptions and tariff benefits, recapture of granted incentives, and a defective AML/UBO record that impairs banking and audit clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Registers, Minute Book, and Corporate Records Annual Readiness Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office; court registry for member/manager registration changes when they occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Maintained continuously and made current by 31 March of each year as a corporate-secretarial governance standard; any member/manager change is filed with the competent registry office within 1 month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Missing or inaccurate statutory registers invalidate a filing party's good-faith reliance, obstruct court registration changes, expose managers to non-criminal fines up to KRW 5 million, and constitute a governance red flag during external audit and AML due diligence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Corporations, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint an independent certified CPA auditor when total assets at the fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million). The obligation also applies to listed or publicly designated companies and to companies specifically ordered by the Financial Services Commission due to debt ratio, industry risk, or investor-protection concerns. Korea does not impose a statutory audit solely on the basis of turnover or headcount; the quantitative threshold is balance-sheet assets.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed and FSS-designated companies; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean GAAP for general companies (K-GAAP / General Enterprise Accounting Standards) or approved SME accounting standards. The external audit must be performed in accordance with KICPA Standards on Auditing and the external audit guidance issued by the Financial Supervisory Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate an annual online UBO return for every private Yuhan Hoesa; instead, the company must keep an accurate and current register of members at its registered office. A transfer of membership or equity interest is effective only upon entry in the member register, and any change for a foreign-invested enterprise must be reported to KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank within 30 days. In addition, the annual foreign-invested enterprise status report confirms the beneficial ownership structure by 31 March. Financial institutions and external auditors require a demonstrably current beneficial-owner identification file under Korea's AML obligations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national CIT on taxable income over KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 26.4% aggregate top statutory rate; progressive national rates are 9% on income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on the next tranche up to KRW 20 billion, and 21% on the next tranche up to KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years followed by a 50% reduction for the following 2 years for qualifying high-tech foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones; SME preferential rates and special credits for facility and future-growth investment; no general patent box, but qualifying technology-transfer income may benefit from a special reduced rate or tax credit
